title_en: Spring Cleaning Before the New Year's Eve Dinner
note_en: 反而 marks a result that goes against what you'd expect: 结果画蛇添足，味道反而变差了 "he overdid it, and the soup actually tasted worse." English uses "actually," "instead" or "if anything," often at the start of the clause, but 反而 is an adverb and sits right before the verb or adjective, after the subject: 爸爸反而比谁都积极 "Dad, of all people, became the keenest."
